newsitem.title: SPAIN: Endesa, Sevilla and Fecsa resume trading firmer.
newsitem.headline: Endesa, Sevilla and Fecsa resume trading firmer.

text.p: Spain's Endesa, Fecsa and Sevillana resumed trading at higher prices after Endesa announced it would launch a buy offer for the other two electricity firms.
Endesa resumed trading at 8,100 pesetas after being suspended earlier pending the announcement of the buy offer. This was up 1.8 percent on Thursday's closing price of 7,950 pesetas.
Sevillana was trading at 1,255, up 7.7 percent on Thursday's close, after Endesa announced it would buy up to 75 percent of the firm at 1,300 pesetas per share.
The Andalusian company said its board considered the offer friendly and would recommend its shareholders accept it. Endesa currently holds 39.4 percent of Sevillana.

Fecsa was up 7 percent at 1,070 after Endesa said it would also buy up to 75 percent of its social capital, but at 1,100 pesetas per share. The state-owned electrical group already holds a 49 percent stake in Fecsa.
